name: Hearing (samāʿ)
definition: What has been heard from the Arabs whose speech counts as evidence: the Qurʾān, the speech of the Prophet as far as its wording is sure, and the poetry and prose of the Arabs of the age of evidence.
body: Samāʿ, also called naql (transmission), is the first source of grammar: a rule stands only on what the Arabs were heard to say. The grammarians drew a line in time and place, the 'age of evidence': the poets down to about the middle of the second/eighth century, and the Bedouin of the desert whose speech had not mixed with that of the cities. Al-Kisāʾī's fifteen bottles of ink, filled among the Bedouin of Najd and the Ḥijāz, and the Bedouin called in at the masʾala zunbūriyya, belong to this search.

What is heard is weighed: a usage heard often is followed and may be extended by analogy (qiyās); one heard rarely is kept to the words heard and called shādhdh or nādir. The Kufans were readier than the Basrans to build a rule on a single report, which is one of the main differences between the schools.
